name: Burkinabe Riz Gras
description: Riz gras, meaning 'fat rice' in French, is Burkina Faso's national dish, its name genuinely referring to the real generous amount of oil used - real technique blends onion, garlic, tomato, and chili together first, then fries this puree until it visibly reduces, darkens, and the oil separates at the edges, the same fry-down principle behind jollof.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

ingredients_full.note: tbsp, generous - the real amount that gives the dish its name

steps_detailed: Blend the tomatoes, half the onion, garlic, and jalapeño into a smooth puree.
Brown the chicken in the oil, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the remaining onion in the same oil, add the tomato paste, cook 2 minutes.
Add the blended puree and fry, uncovered, 12-15 minutes, until it visibly reduces, darkens, and the oil separates at the edges - this real fry-down is what defines riz gras.
Stir in the rice, broth, and chicken, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.

name: Burkinabe Tô
description: Tô (also called saghbo), a thick porridge made from millet, sorghum, or maize flour, is Burkina Faso's most essential staple, real technique stirring vigorously and continuously to build its real stiff, dippable texture.

name: Burkinabe Babenda
description: Babenda, bitter greens cooked with rice and pounded peanuts, genuinely originated as a resourceful dish from lean harvest years - real versions include soumbala, fermented locust bean, which isn't a distinct item here, so this version leans on the greens and peanuts alone, missing soumbala's real pungent, almost blue-cheese-like depth.

name: Burkinabe Ragout d'Igname (Yam Stew)
description: Ragout d'igname, a yam stew shared across the wider West African region, real technique keeping the seasoning simple - just salt and pepper - so the real flavor of the vegetables carries the dish.
steps_detailed: Simmer the yam, carrot, bell pepper, garlic, ginger, and pepper together in 2 cups water 25-28 minutes until the yam is tender, being generous with the black pepper.

name: Burkinabe Maafe
description: Maafe (tigadeguena), meat stewed in a rich peanut sauce, is a beloved dish across Burkina Faso and the wider region, real technique whisking the peanut butter slowly to keep the sauce smooth.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter slowly with the tomatoes and a little water, add to the pot.
Add the carrot and simmer 30-35 minutes until the beef is tender.

name: Burkinabe Bissap
description: Bissap, a hibiscus drink often served with pineapple, is one of Burkina Faso's most popular beverages.
steps_detailed: Warm the hibiscus tea and stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Chill, then serve over ice with the pineapple chunks.

name: Burkinabe Grilled Chicken
description: Grilled chicken generously seasoned with garlic and pepper, a beloved Burkinabe dish for gatherings.
steps_detailed: Rub the chicken with the garlic and pepper, being generous with both.
Grill, turning, 12-15 minutes, until charred and cooked through.

description: Fried ripe plantain, a common Burkinabe side dish, real versions using genuinely ripe plantain for real caramelization.

description: A simple tomato and onion salad, a common Burkinabe side, real technique letting the onion sit briefly in lemon juice first.

Simmer 12-15 minutes until thickened.
